domain_title: Architecture, security, robustness, safety and evaluation
title: Safety, failure handling and recovery
canonical_definition: Foreseeable unsafe states are constrained through fail-safe behavior, interruption, fallback, rollback, human takeover, incident response and recovery testing.

conditions: All systems; stronger requirements for autonomous, safety-relevant, high-availability or consequential uses.
Record the assessed release, operating scope and evidence that supports any applicability decision.

primary_questions.question: Are failure modes, unsafe states, recovery objectives and control-transfer conditions defined?
Are fail-safe states, interruption, fallback, rollback, human takeover and incident procedures implemented?
Do fault-injection, recovery and operational exercises demonstrate controlled degradation and timely restoration?

conditions: Refer a material failure of safety, failure handling and recovery to the accountable authority before a consequential transition.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: NIST AI 100-1, MEASURE 2.6 (PDF p. 35), MANAGE 2.3 (PDF p. 37), MANAGE 2.4 (PDF p. 37)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: The voluntary framework provides guidance on evaluating safety and planning response, recovery and disengagement. The SAE criteria define the object-specific rules. Confirm any binding obligation through the accountable authority and its applicable source.

governance_purpose: Make safety, failure handling and recovery verifiable against the current AI system, decision context and accountable ownership.
distinct_claim: D5 evaluates safety, failure handling and recovery using evidence from intent through operation. AP-D5 independently assesses evidence of fail-open ai operation.

atomic_subcriteria.criterion: The versioned definition identifies a failure and recovery plan defining unsafe states, stop thresholds, fallback limits and human transfer. Record the accountable owner, scope and material assumptions.

The current release demonstrates enforced safe-state transition, bounded retries, interruption, rollback, recovery permissions and incident notification. Trace the decisions and controls to attributable records.

Representative, executed evidence provides controlled fault exercises and real incident records showing interruption, safe degradation and restoration within objectives. Compare expected and observed outcomes and record exceptions.
For an operating system, current records cover the material paths involved in safety, failure handling and recovery, including relevant exceptions and changes.

required_evidence.title: Versioned scope and control definition
required_evidence.description: Provide a failure and recovery plan defining unsafe states, stop thresholds, fallback limits and human transfer. Include the affected workflow, current version and accountable owner.

required_evidence.title: Effective implementation records
required_evidence.description: Demonstrate enforced safe-state transition, bounded retries, interruption, rollback, recovery permissions and incident notification. Trace the scope, control and authority to the current implementation, including exceptions.

required_evidence.title: Representative verification results
required_evidence.description: Provide controlled fault exercises and real incident records showing interruption, safe degradation and restoration within objectives. Include current version, test scope, criteria, expected and observed outcomes, and unresolved failures.

required_evidence.title: Current operating or change evidence
required_evidence.description: Retain dated records that show how safety, failure handling and recovery works for the assessed scope, including the relevant exceptions and any material change since the evidence was captured.

sufficiency: Start with a failure and recovery plan defining unsafe states, stop thresholds, fallback limits and human transfer. Reconcile it against the effective controls and representative results for the same operating scope and version.

Use controlled fault exercises and real incident records showing interruption, safe degradation and restoration within objectives to support effectiveness at the relevant lifecycle stage. Record missing paths and unresolved conflicts as UNKNOWN. A verified shortfall can support a gap without resolving the other questions.
Reassess affected evidence after a material change. An accountable human validates or approves the result where required by the lifecycle target.
evidence_rules.evidence_ceiling: A specification supports DECLARED intent. Effective implementation records may support IMPLEMENTED. Representative executed tests support TESTED within their scope. Current operating evidence supports OPERATIONALLY_OBSERVED for covered paths and time. Record human assurance independently.
false_positive_guards: A fallback is justified when the permitted degraded scope, control checks and accountable recovery route are evidenced.
Reconcile document claims with the effective release, actual operation and relevant exceptions before recording satisfaction.
prohibited_inferences: A capability gap alone cannot establish AP-D5 presence.
An approved design or evidence plan cannot establish test execution or operational effectiveness.
Satisfying this capability cannot by itself authorize progression or establish legal compliance.

finding_definitions.title: Material definition or intent gap in safety, failure handling and recovery
Verified implementation or effectiveness gap in safety, failure handling and recovery
Evidence remains insufficient for safety, failure handling and recovery in the assessed scope
